```r
library(rgeomex)
library(ggplot2)
```

`extract_blocks()` extracts the blocks that intersect the boundary of a locality. It has two arguments: the state key (`cve_edo`) and the name of the locality (`locality`). It returns a list with two sf objects: `locality` (the boundary of the locality) and `block`.

Only the file of the requested state is downloaded.

## Mérida


```r
merida <- extract_blocks(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")
nrow(merida$block)
#> [1] 15374
```


```r
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = merida$block, fill = "#E01A59", col = "white", lwd = 0.05) +
  geom_sf(data = merida$locality, fill = NA, col = "black", lwd = 0.3) +
  theme_void()
```

<img src="figures/extract_blocks_en-merida_map-1.png" alt="merida_map" width="100%" />

## Guadalajara




## Step by step

The same steps the function does:


```r
# 1. the locality
loc <- extract_locality(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")

# 2. the dataset of the state
x <- rgeomex_load("blocks_ine20_mx", cve_edo = "31") |>
  sf::st_make_valid()

# 3. what intersects the locality
x <- x[loc, ]
nrow(x)
#> [1] 15374
```
